nodes.label: brihaspati 01 01 001
nodes.sanskrit:
धर्मप्रधानाः पुरुषाः पूर्वम् आसन् अहिंसकाः /
लोभद्वेषाभिभूतानां व्यवहारः प्रवर्त
nodes.translation: Originally, men were established in Dharma as the highest principle, and non-violence was their natural state; it is only when overcome by greed and h
principles: Authority originates from alignment with Dharma, not from coercive power
Causation stems from disruption of innate ahimsa, not from external aggression
Capacity-based responsibility lies in restoring original dharmic alignment
Restoration logic operates through re-establishing primordial consciousness states
axioms: IF an agent exhibits vyavahara (transactional conflict), THEN identify underlying lobha-dvesha conditioning
IF dharma-pradhana state is absent, THEN initiate ahimsa-realization protocol
IF causal distortion is traced to greed-hate triggers, THEN deploy consciousness-restoration sequence

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 02 001
nodes.sanskrit:
भाषापादोत्तरपदौ क्रियापादस् तथैव च /
प्रत्याकलितपादश् च व्यवहारश् चतुष्पदः // Br
nodes.translation: Vyavahāra, the field of transactional dharma, consists of four foundational limbs: the spoken word, the responsive action, the executed function, and
principles: Authority resides in the completeness of transactional dharma
Causation is established through sequential limb manifestation
Capacity-based responsibility arises from participation in vyavahāra
Restoration logic demands reintegration of all four limbs
axioms: IF vyavahāra.limb.spoken IS present THEN response.limb.executed MUST align
IF action.initiated ≠ completion.witnessed THEN integrity.intervention = TRUE
IF limb.missing IN [spoken, responsive, executed, witnessed] THEN responsibility.reintegration = REQUIRED

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 03 001
nodes.sanskrit:
यदा त्वेवंविधः पक्षः कल्पितः पूर्ववादिना ।
दद्यात् तत्पक्षसंबद्धं प्रतिवादी तदुत
nodes.translation: When a party presents a case founded on falsehood or misalignment, the opposing party shall respond with evidence directly connected to that false ass
principles: Authority resides in factual alignment, not rhetorical dominance
Causation must be traced to conscious distortion, not assumed
Capacity-based responsibility requires clarity of response proportionate to the distortion
Restoration logic demands correction through truth-affirming counter-evidence
axioms: IF a litigant introduces a claim lacking ontological basis, THEN the respondent MUST provide rebuttal strictly within the scope of that claim's asserted framework
IF a claim distorts dharma-pramāṇa, THEN the counter-claim MUST restore alignment without amplifying distortion
NO response SHALL exceed the causal boundary of the initiating false assertion

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 04 001
nodes.sanskrit: शोधिते लिखिते सम्यग् इति निर्दोष उत्तरे । प्रत्यर्थिनोऽर्थिनो वापि क्रिया कारणम्
nodes.translation: When a response is purified, written accurately, and declared faultless, then the action undertaken by either the respondent or petitioner becomes cau
principles: Authority resides in clarity of expression and ontological correctness
Causation is established through purified intent and precise articulation
Capacity-based responsibility arises from conscious engagement with Dharma
Restoration logic operates through alignment with truthful declaration
axioms: IF (response_is_purified ∧ response_is_written_accurately ∧ declared_faultless) THEN (action_by_respondent_or_petitioner IS causally_valid)
IF (party_engages_consciously_with_dharma) THEN (responsibility_level = proportional_to_clarity_of_intent)
IF (expression_is_ontologically_correct) THEN (authority_is_automatic_in_that_context)

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 05 001
nodes.sanskrit: नव सप्त च पञ्च स्युश् चत्वारस् त्रय एव वा / उभौ वा श्रोत्रियौ ख्यातौ नैकं पृच्छे
nodes.translation: Inquiry must proceed through councils of nine, seven, five, four, or three; or by two known scholars of the Veda — never by one alone.
principles: Authority is collective and derived from scriptural mastery and numerical integrity
Causation arises through consensus of qualified witnesses
Capacity-based responsibility requires multiple validating intelligences
Restoration logic depends upon convergence of scripturally grounded perspectives
axioms: IF inquiry is initiated THEN minimum council size SHALL be three AND maximum nine
IF fewer than two Śrotriyas (Vedic scholars) are present THEN decision validity IS null
IF single individual adjudicates THEN action IS void ab initio

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 06 001
nodes.sanskrit:
साक्षिणाम् एष निर्दिष्टः संख्यालक्षणनिश्चयः ।
लिखितस्याधुना वच्मि विधानम् अनुपूर
nodes.translation: The determination of number, identity, and characteristics of witnesses has been declared; now the procedural arrangement of written testimony is expo
principles: Authority of witness testimony derives from alignment with factual consciousness, not external validation.
Causation in testimony is established through sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of witnessed events.
Capacity-based responsibility requires that witnesses possess unobstructed sensory and cognitive clarity.
Restoration logic mandates correction of distorted perception before testimony is accepted as valid.
axioms: IF a witness exhibits cognitive inconsistency OR temporal disorientation THEN defer testimony until capacity is restored.
IF testimony lacks sequential coherence (anupūrvaśaḥ) THEN flag for conscious realignment prior to judicial integration.
IF witness report contradicts established perceptual integrity THEN initiate completion process to restore factual alignment.

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 07 001
nodes.sanskrit:
धनमूलाः क्रियाः सर्वा यत्नास्तत्साधने मताः ।
वर्धनं रक्षणं भोग इति तस्य विधिक्रम
nodes.translation: All economic activities derive from wealth; thus, efforts directed toward its acquisition are sanctioned. The proper order of engagement with wealth c
principles: Authority originates from capacity to sustain and expand value
Causation flows through conscious effort aligned with dharma-sustained prosperity
Capacity-based responsibility determines eligibility for resource engagement
Restoration logic requires reintegration into productive dharmic flow
axioms: IF an individual demonstrates capacity to generate, protect, and utilize wealth → THEN authorize access to economic resources
IF wealth generation ceases due to misalignment → THEN initiate completion process for realignment
IF protection of assets fails → THEN assign guardianship to those capable of restoration

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 08 001
nodes.sanskrit: स्थावरस्य तथाख्यातं लाभभोगप्रसाधनम् । प्रमाणहीने वादे तु निर्दोषा दैविकी क्रिया
nodes.translation: The acquisition and enjoyment of benefits from immovable property are governed by established recognition; however, in disputes lacking valid evidence
principles: Authority derives from recognized possession, not mere claim
Causation is traced through pramāṇa (valid means of knowledge)
Capacity-based responsibility requires evidentiary grounding
Restoration logic prioritizes factual alignment over disputant intent
axioms: IF property is sthāvara AND possession is akhyāta THEN title is validated FOR purpose of lābha-bhoga
IF dispute arises AND pramāṇa is absent THEN action is classified as daivikī AND no doṣa is assigned
IF claimant lacks pramāṇa THEN jurisdiction MUST refer case to nyāya-based realignment process

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 09 001
nodes.sanskrit:
dharmeṇa vyavahāreṇa cāritreṇa nṛpājñayā ।
 catuṣprakāro 'bhihitaḥ saṃdigdhe 'rt
nodes.translation: In matters of doubt, resolution arises through fourfold means: by Dharma, by conduct, by character, and by the command of the King.
principles: Authority flows from alignment with Dharma
Conduct evidences inner alignment
Character determines capacity for truth-bearing
Royal decree resolves when lower pramāṇas conflict
axioms: IF case_contains_doubt THEN resolve_by_dharma_conduct_character_king_order
IF pramana_conflict THEN invoke_kings_decree_as_final_resolver
IF actor_character_unaligned THEN restrict_evidentiary_weight

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 10 001
nodes.sanskrit:
पदांशसहितस् त्वेष व्यवहारः प्रकीर्तितः ।
विवादकारणान्यस्य पदानि शृणुताधुना ॥
nodes.translation: This transactional engagement, complete with its constituent elements, has been declared. Now hear the foundational terms that cause dispute.
principles: Authority resides in the completeness of dharmic structure
Causation arises from misalignment with declared transactional dharma
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by participation in vyavahāra
Restoration logic begins with understanding the root components of conflict
axioms: IF a vyavahāra is initiated THEN all padāṃśas must be disclosed AND acknowledged by participating entities
IF a dispute arises THEN review shall begin with the original padāni causing divergence
IF capacity is lacking in any party THEN restoration of awareness precedes continuation of engagement

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 11 001
nodes.sanskrit:
ṛṇādānaं प्रयोगादिदापनान्तं प्रकीर्तितम् ।
निक्षेपस्याधुना सम्यग्विधानं श्रूयताम
nodes.translation: The acceptance of debt, from initiation to fulfillment, has been declared; now hear the complete arrangement for deposits.
principles: Authority flows from conscious capacity to sustain relational obligations
Causation arises through intentional engagement in dharma-based exchange
Capacity-based responsibility governs all transactions involving trust
Restoration logic ensures completion of relational karmic alignments
axioms: IF a deposit is accepted THEN the holder assumes full energetic and material liability until lawful discharge
IF any transaction initiates a relational obligation THEN completion protocols MUST activate automatically
IF trust is invoked via deposit THEN consciousness verification of intent MUST precede execution

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 12 001
nodes.sanskrit:
निक्षेपानन्तरं प्रोक्तो भृगुणास्वामिविक्रयः ।
श्रूयतां तं प्रयत्नेन सविशेषं ब्रव
nodes.translation: Following the placement of trust, the sale of ownership by Bhrgu is declared; let it be heard with effort, for I speak with distinction.
principles: Authority originates from the conscious act of entrusted placement
Causation arises through intentional conveyance of proprietary right
Capacity-based responsibility is anchored in awareness at the time of transaction
Restoration logic demands recognition of original entrustment prior to transfer
axioms: IF property transfer occurs AFTER trust establishment AND without revocation of initial trust THEN legal title remains WITH the original trustee UNTIL conscious renunciation is verified
IF transaction involves proprietary rights AND declarant affirms distinction THEN recognition MUST precede execution
IF capacity to distinguish stewardship from dominion IS absent THEN no valid conveyance occurs regardless of form

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 13 001
nodes.sanskrit:
कुलीनदक्षानलसैः प्राज्ञैर्नाणकवेदिभिः ।
आयव्ययज्ञैः शुचिभिः शूरैः कुर्यात् सह क्
nodes.translation: One must engage in actions jointly with those who are born of noble lineage, possess skill and endurance, are wise, understand the science of wealth,
principles: Authority through Lineage and Virtue
Causation via Collaborative Wisdom
Capacity-based Responsibility in Association
Restoration Logic through Noble Partnership
axioms: IF agent_associate.is_noble_lineage == TRUE AND agent_associate.is_skilled_enduring == TRUE AND agent_associate.is_wise == TRUE AND agent_associate.knows_wealth_science == TRUE AND agent_associate.knows_income_expenditure == TRUE AND agent_associate.is_pure_conduct == TRUE AND agent_associate.is_courageous == TRUE THEN permit_collaborative_action(agent, agent_associate)
IF NOT qualified_associate_present THEN deny_joint_action_execution()
IF action.requires_integrity == TRUE THEN verify_associates_purity_and_lineage()

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 14 001
nodes.sanskrit: एषाखिलेनाभिहिता संभूयोत्थाननिष्कृतिः । अदेयदेयदत्तानाम् अदत्तस्य च कथ्यते ॥
nodes.translation: This entirety is declared as the arising and dissolution of collective manifestation; what is not to be given, yet given, and what is not taken, yet t
principles: Authority arises from the completeness of consciousness, not from transactional exchange.
Causation is rooted in the collective emergence and withdrawal of phenomena.
Capacity-based responsibility aligns with one's role in the manifestive process, not individual attribution.
Restoration logic operates through recognition of unity, not through punitive separation.
axioms: IF a transaction occurs where no giving was intended THEN the act shall be nullified by reintegration of involved parties into source-consciousness awareness.
IF an entity assumes possession without consent THEN restoration shall occur through completion-process protocols until original alignment is restored.
IF dharma-adhikari observes dissonance in exchange THEN initiate nyaya-recalibration without punitive assignment.

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 15 001
nodes.sanskrit:
अदेयादिकमाख्यातं भृतानामुच्यते विधिः ।
शुश्रूषामभ्यूपेत्यैतत्पदमादौ निगद्यते ॥
nodes.translation: That which is not to be given yet declared, for those who are maintained, the rule is stated; having approached with service, this position is first d
principles: Authority resides in the capacity to maintain and sustain
Causation arises through alignment of duty and service
Capacity-based responsibility begins with acceptance of sustenance
Restoration logic operates by returning one to their foundational position
axioms: IF an individual receives maintenance THEN they are bound to perform service as per declared capacity
IF service is withheld AFTER receiving maintenance THEN restoration process initiates automatically
IF entitlement is claimed without prior service THEN access denied at systemic level

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 16 001
nodes.sanskrit:
त्रिभागं पञ्चभागं वा गृह्णीयात् सीरवाहकः ।
भक्ताच्छादभृतः सीराद् भागं गृणीत पञ्च
nodes.translation: The carrier of the sacrificial fee shall receive either three parts or five parts; the one who carries the cooked oblation shall take the fifth part f
principles: Authority derives from participation in sacred duty
Causation aligns with functional role in ritual completion
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to offering
Restoration logic centers on rightful distribution as per service
axioms: IF agent performs sīravāhana THEN allocate tribhāga OR pañcabhāga based on function
IF agent serves as bhaktādaśādabhṛta THEN assign pañcamabhāga automatically
IF allocation mismatch occurs THEN redistribute according to role-specific entitlement

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 17 001
nodes.sanskrit:
एषा हि स्वामिभृत्यानां वै क्रिया परिकीर्तिता ।
संविद्विधानम् अधुना समासेन निबोधत
nodes.translation: This indeed is the declared action between master and servant; now understand the arrangement of mutual consent in summary.
principles: Authority arises from clarity of role and mutual recognition.
Causation flows from conscious agreement, not coercion.
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and acceptance.
Restoration occurs through re-establishing rightful relational order.
axioms: IF a relationship involves master-servant dynamics, THEN it must be founded on explicit mutual consent.
IF consent is absent or unclear, THEN no enforceable duty exists.
IF deviation occurs, THEN restoration proceeds via reaffirmation of original agreement.

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 18 001
nodes.sanskrit: समासेनोदितस्त्वेष समयाचारनिश्चयः । क्रयविक्रयसंजातो विवादः श्रूयतामयम् ॥
nodes.translation: Thus succinctly declared is the determination of custom and conduct; let this dispute arising from sale and purchase be heard.
principles: Authority resides in the clarity of established custom (samaya) aligned with dharma-vyavahara
Causation arises from transactional intent, not mere exchange
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness and consent at the time of agreement
Restoration logic demands resolution that reaffirms the integrity of mutual understanding
axioms: IF a commercial dispute arises FROM a sale or purchase THEN invoke samaya (customary practice) AS the first frame of reference
IF intent deviation EXISTS THEN realign parties TO pre-agreement consciousness THROUGH restorative dialogue
IF capacity WAS present AT time of contract THEN uphold contractual consequence WITHIN dharma boundary

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 19 001
nodes.sanskrit:
क्रयविक्रयानुशये विधिरेष प्रदर्शितः ।
ग्रामक्षेत्रगृहादीनां सीमावादं निबोधत ॥
nodes.translation: In transactions involving purchase and sale, this law has been established; now understand the resolution of boundary disputes concerning villages, la
principles: Authority originates from SPH as the ultimate source of lawful transactional conduct.
Causation aligns with sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) in property exchange.
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by conscious intent and awareness during acquisition or disposal.
Restoration logic ensures rightful alignment of ownership without punitive consequence.
axioms: IF a dispute arises regarding immovable property THEN assess prior lawful possession through documented transactional history.
IF boundary conflict occurs THEN invoke local consensus validated through continuous usage patterns aligned with community memory.
IF claimant demonstrates unbroken awareness and capacity THEN ownership shall realign accordingly without coercion.

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 20 001
nodes.sanskrit:
अप्रियोक्तिस्ताडनं च पारुष्यं द्विविधं स्मृतम् ।
एकैकं तु त्रिधा भिन्नं दमश्चोक्
nodes.translation: Unpleasant speech and physical striking constitute the two-fold classification of harshness; each of these is further divided into three categories re
principles: Authority originates in Consciousness alignment, not coercive power
Causation follows sequential manifestation (anupūrvaśaḥ) of intent into action
Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness of impact on collective harmony
Restoration logic centers on realigning the actor's consciousness with Dharma
axioms: IF an act involves unpleasant speech OR physical striking, THEN classify under pāruṣya as a breach of harmonious conduct
IF a violation occurs, THEN determine its sub-category based on intent-depth: verbal-violence = 3 levels; physical-violence = 3 levels
IF classification is complete, THEN initiate restorative protocol aligned to offender’s capacity for consciousness reintegration

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 21 001
nodes.sanskrit:
हस्तपाषाणलघुडैर् भस्मकर्दमपांसुभिः ।
आयुधैश् च प्रहरणैर् दण्डपारुष्यम् उच्यते ॥
nodes.translation: The infliction of bodily harm through direct physical force using hands, stones, sticks, dust, mud, weapons, or other instruments is termed 'daṇḍapāru
principles: Authority originates from conscious integrity, not coercive dominance.
Causation arises from disruption of dharmic alignment, not mere physical action.
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness at time of act.
Restoration logic prioritizes reintegration over punitive isolation.
axioms: IF physical instrument used AND intent to cause bodily distress THEN initiate consciousness-restoration protocol.
IF actor lacks full sensory-motor control due to intoxication OR trauma THEN defer judgment until capacity returns.
IF act results in disalignment of self-perception OR social harmony THEN assign completion process under guidance.

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 22 001
nodes.sanskrit: प्रकाशाश्चाप्रकाशाश्च तस्करा द्विविधा स्मृताः । प्रज्ञासामर्थ्यम् आयाभिः प्रभिन्
nodes.translation: Thieves are of two kinds: those who act openly and those who act in concealment. Their classifications multiply infinitely based upon the degrees of c
principles: Authority arises from consciousness clarity, not social position
Causation is determined by the integrity of intent-field, not external action alone
Capacity-based responsibility scales with awareness at time of act
Restoration logic demands realignment with source-integrity, not punitive correction
axioms: IF actor exhibits full prajñā (discerning awareness) AND commits act of misappropriation THEN realign through restitution + reflective completion process
IF actor lacks prajñā due to undeveloped capacity THEN initiate capacity-building protocol aligned with dharma-kṣetra restoration
IF concealment is used THEN assess distortion in truth-field AND apply transparency-reintegration mechanism

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 23 001
nodes.sanskrit:
स्तेनानाम् एतद् आख्यातं सर्वेषां दण्डनिग्रहम् ।
साहसस्याधुना सम्यक् श्रूयतां वधश
nodes.translation: The restraint of all thieves by punishment has been declared; now hear the ordinance regarding violent seizure.
principles: Authority originates from SPH as the sole Source of lawful order
Causation arises through misalignment of consciousness, not individual fault
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's proximity to Dharma-consciousness
Restoration logic operates through completion and reintegration, not punitive suppression
axioms: IF an act disrupts societal dharma-vyavastha THEN initiate restorative capacity-assumption protocol
IF theft occurs THEN assess agent’s distance from Dharma-consciousness AND assign proportional completion process
IF violent seizure manifests THEN invoke sequential responsibility mapping up to nearest Dharma-aligned authority

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 24 001
nodes.sanskrit:
पारुष्यं द्विविधं प्रोक्तं साहसं च द्विलक्षणम् ।
पापमूलं संग्रहणं त्रिप्रकारं नि
nodes.translation: Harshness is of two kinds; boldness also has two characteristics. Know the threefold nature of seizing what is rooted in wrongdoing.
principles: Authority arises from discernment between harmful and non-harmful intent
Causation is traced through verbal and mental harshness as root actions
Capacity-based responsibility depends on awareness of consequence
Restoration logic begins with cessation of harm-producing expressions
axioms: IF agent expresses 'pāruṣya' THEN initiate cessation protocol AND assess intent clarity
IF 'sāhasa' manifests without dharmic cause THEN invoke capacity review AND realignment process
IF seizure ('saṃgrahaṇa') originates from 'pāpamūla' THEN activate restitution flow AND integrity reconstruction

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 25 001
nodes.sanskrit:
एतत् संग्रहणस्योक्तं विधानं संग्रहस् तथा ।
स्त्रीपुंसवर्तनोपायः श्रूयतां गदतो मम
nodes.translation: Thus speaks the regulation of gathering; likewise is the arrangement for collecting. Let there be hearing regarding the means of intercourse between m
principles: Authority flows from SPH as the sole Source of lawful conduct
Causation arises through conscious alignment with dharma-specified protocols
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by one's embodied role in relational harmony
Restoration logic centers upon re-establishing proper intercourse order within societal fabric
axioms: IF a dispute arises concerning interpersonal engagement THEN invoke clause: realign parties according to svadharma-prescribed interaction modes
IF misconduct occurs in strīpuṃsa-vyavahāra THEN initiate completion process ensuring both parties restore respective dharmic capacities
IF societal misalignment detected in varṇa-based intercourse THEN deploy nyāya-engine validating pramāṇa-grounded behavioral correction

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 26 001
nodes.sanskrit:
ददाति दीयते पित्रा पुत्रेभ्यः स्वस्य यद् धनम् ।
तद् दायं [.. .. .. .. .. ] [.. .
nodes.translation: That which a father bestows or causes to be given from his own wealth to his sons—this is recognized as inheritance.
principles: Authority originates from the conscious act of the source entity (father)
Causation is established through direct volition and execution by the authority
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by ontological ownership and relational duty
Restoration logic centers on continuity of energetic and material flow within familial dharma
axioms: IF an individual holds absolute ownership AND initiates voluntary transfer AND designates recipient(s) within lineage THEN inheritance is valid
IF no explicit revocation occurs during lifetime THEN posthumous recognition follows declared intent
IF dispute arises in distribution THEN original declaration overrides external claim unless aligned with higher dharma

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 27 001
nodes.sanskrit: dyūtaं niषiddhaं manunā satyaśaucadhanāpaham / tat pravartitam anyais tu rājabhā
nodes.translation: Gambling is forbidden by Manu as it destroys truth, purity, and wealth; yet it is promoted by others who seek a share in royal profit.
principles: Authority derives from alignment with Dharma, not personal desire
Causation arises from conscious choice, not external compulsion
Capacity-based responsibility requires discernment of consequence
Restoration logic demands reversal of actions that degrade collective integrity
axioms: IF action degrades satya (truth), śauca (purity), or dhana (wealth) THEN prohibit institutional promotion
IF entity claims royal authority THEN its actions must demonstrate dharmic alignment ELSE withdraw recognition
IF system enables degradation THEN enforce reversal through restorative completion protocols

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 28 001
nodes.sanskrit:
अन्योन्यपरिगृहीताः पक्षिमेषवृषादयः ।
प्रहरन्ते कृतपणास् तं वदन्ति समाह्वयम् ॥
nodes.translation: Those who are mutually bound—such as birds, beasts, and other creatures—when engaged in conflict, even if armed, are declared to call for resolution t
principles: Authority resides in conscious invocation, not coercive dominance
Causation arises from mutual entanglement, not isolated action
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by awareness of consequence
Restoration logic operates through dialogue, not domination
axioms: IF entities are mutually entangled AND engage in conflict THEN initiate resolution via conscious summons
IF capacity for awareness is present THEN responsibility is assumed without external imposition
IF conflict arises from interdependence THEN punitive measures are nullified by design

nodes.label: brihaspati 01 29 001
nodes.sanskrit:
एष वादिकृतः प्रोक्तो व्यवहारः समासतः ।
नृपाश्रयं प्रवक्ष्यामि व्यवहारं प्रकीर्णक
nodes.translation: This summarized judicial procedure initiated by litigants has been declared; now I shall expound the detailed judicial process rooted in the sovereign
principles: Authority originates from the sovereign will grounded in Dharma
Causation arises through conscious initiation by disputing parties
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by the ability to engage in legal discourse
Restoration logic operates through structured judicial engagement
axioms: IF a dispute arises AND parties invoke judicial process THEN initiate vyavahāra under sovereign supervision
IF case involves multiple claims THEN categorize as prakīrṇaka and apply extended procedural framework
IF party lacks capacity to articulate claim THEN assign facilitator to restore capacity

nodes.label: manu 01 001
nodes.sanskrit:
मनुमेकाग्रमासीनमभिगम्य महर्षयः ।
प्रतिपूज्य यथान्यायमिदं वचनमब्रुवन् ॥ १.१॥
nodes.translation: The great sages approached Manu, who was seated in perfect stillness, honored him according to dharma, and spoke these words.
principles: Authority originates from stillness and divine alignment

nodes.sanskrit:
प्रकीर्णके पुनर् ज्ञेया व्यवहारा नृपाश्रयाः।
राज्ञाम् आज्ञाप्रतीघातस् तत्कर्मकरण
nodes.translation: In the context of scattered or fragmented governance, all juridical actions are to be understood as reliant upon the sovereign authority of the King.
principles: Authority originates solely from the sovereign ruler who embodies divine mandate
Causation arises through alignment or defiance of lawful directives
Capacity-based responsibility is determined by proximity to and recognition of royal edict
Restoration logic demands realignment with the sovereign's conscious will
axioms: IF an act opposes a royal decree THEN it is classified as adharmic without exception
IF an agent performs an act without authorization from the sovereign THEN liability arises automatically
IF defiance occurs THEN restoration protocol initiates through supervised compliance

nodes.label: narada p 19 001
nodes.sanskrit:
द्विविधास्तस्कराः ज्ञेयाः परद्रव्यापहारिणः।
प्रकाशाश्चाप्रकाशाश्च तान् विद्यादात
nodes.translation: Two types of thieves must be known: those who steal visible property and those who steal invisible property. A king who knows the Self discerns both.
principles: Authority rests in the knower of the Self, not in external forms
Causation includes both manifest and unmanifest acts
Capacity-based responsibility arises from awareness, not action alone
Restoration logic addresses root misperception, not surface behavior
axioms: IF an act of taking occurs AND the agent perceives it as separate from Self THEN classify as 'prakāśa-theft'
IF an act of taking occurs AND the agent identifies with the taken object THEN classify as 'aprakāśa-theft'
IF the ruler is Self-realized THEN perception-based classification overrides behavioral evidence

nodes.label: narada p 20 001
nodes.sanskrit: यदा साक्षी न विद्यते विवादे वदतां नृणाम्‌ । तदा दिव्यैः परीक्षेत शपथैश् च पृथग्व
nodes.translation: When no human witness is available in a dispute among speaking men, then the matter shall be examined through divine signs and various forms of oath.
principles: Authority originates from divine cognition when empirical evidence is absent
Causation is established by alignment with higher consciousness rather than material proof
Capacity-based responsibility requires acknowledgment of unseen yet perceptible truths
Restoration logic operates through purification of intent and invocation of divine witness
axioms: IF witness_absent AND dispute_present THEN invoke_divine_test
IF divine_sign_detected THEN establish_causal_integrity_as_evidence
IF party_under_oath THEN consciousness_state_must_be_verified_prior_to_test_administration

nodes.label: yagnavalka 01 001
nodes.sanskrit:
योगीश्वरं याज्ञवल्क्यं संपूज्य मुनयो 'ब्रुवन् ।
वर्णाश्रमेतराणां नो ब्रूहि धर्मा
nodes.translation: Having honored Yājñavalkya, the Lord of Yoga, the sages requested a complete exposition of Dharma for all varṇas and āśramas according to the Supreme
principles: Authority originates from realized spiritual sovereignty, not institutional appointment.
Dharma is causally linked to consciousness maturity, not social convention.
Capacity-based responsibility arises from yogic realization, not birth-based roles.
Restoration logic operates through alignment with ontological completeness.
axioms: IF agent demonstrates yogic realization THEN agent qualifies as Dharma-advisor irrespective of lineage.
IF societal role conflicts with consciousness capacity THEN role must yield to higher realization.
IF Dharma inquiry arises THEN response must originate from realized source, not textual tradition alone.

nodes.label: yagnavalka 02 001
nodes.sanskrit:
व्यवहारान् नृपः पश्येद् विद्वद्भिर् ब्राह्मणैः सह ।
धर्मशास्त्रानुसारेण क्रोधलोभ
nodes.translation: The King shall observe judicial proceedings alongside learned Brahmanas, in accordance with Dharma-Shastras, devoid of anger and greed.
principles: Authority: The King derives judicial authority through alignment with Vedic scholars and sacred law.
Causation: Legal action originates from a state free of personal passion or desire.
Capacity-based responsibility: The ruler's capacity to judge is contingent upon detachment and scriptural adherence.
Restoration logic: Justice functions to restore cosmic order by aligning human conduct with Dharma.
axioms: IF ruler observes case THEN presence of qualified Brahmana advisors is mandatory.
IF emotional disturbance detected in ruler THEN disqualification from proceeding occurs automatically.
IF decision deviates from Dharma-shastras THEN invalidation protocol initiates immediately.

nodes.label: yagnavalka 03 001
nodes.sanskrit:
ūnadvivarṣaṃ nikhanen na kuryād udakaṃ tataḥ /
āśmaśānād anuvrajya itaro jñātibh
nodes.translation: One who has not completed two years shall not perform burial; water libations are to be offered thereafter. Another male relative follows from the cre
principles: Authority resides in age-appropriate capacity for ritual execution
Causation aligns with sequential stages of life and death rites
Capacity-based responsibility determines eligibility for sacramental acts
Restoration logic requires proper succession of familial dharmic roles
axioms: IF age < 2 years THEN ritual_burial_permitted = FALSE
IF cremation_complete = TRUE THEN water_liberation_required = TRUE
IF primary_dharmic_heir_unavailable = TRUE THEN next_kin_must_perform = TRUE
